In [[geometry]], the '''gyroelongated square bicupola''' is the [[Johnson solid]] constructed by attaching two [[Square cupola|square cupolae]] on each base of [[octagonal antiprism]]. It has the property of [[Chirality (mathematics)|chirality]].
[[File:J45 gyroelongated square bicupola.stl|thumb|3D model of a gyroelongated square bicupola]]

== Construction ==
The gyroelongated square bicupola is constructed by attaching two [[Square cupola|square cupolae]] on each base of [[octagonal antiprism]], a process known as [[gyroelongation]]. This construction involves the removal of [[octagons]], and replacing them with cupolae.{{r|rajwade}} As a result, this polyhedron has twenty-four triangular and ten square faces.{{r|berman}} The Johnson solid is the convex polyhedron with all of its faces [[Regular polygon|regular]], and the gyroelongated square bicupola is one of them, enumerated as <math> J_{45} </math>.{{r|francis}}

== Properties ==
Given that the edge length <math> a </math>, the surface area is:
<math display="block"> \left(10+6\sqrt{3}\right) a^2 \approx 20.392a^2,</math>
the total area of twenty equilateral triangles and ten squares. Its volume is:
<math display="block"> \left(2+\frac{4}{3}\sqrt{2} + \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{4+2\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{146+103\sqrt{2}}}\right) a^3 \approx 8.154a^3, </math>
the total volume of two square cupolae and an octagonal antiprism.{{r|berman}} Its [[dihedral angles]] can be calculated by adding the components of cupolae and antiprism. The dihedral angle of antiprism between two adjacent triangles is approximately <math> 153.9^\circ </math>. The dihedral angle of each cupola between two squares is <math> 135^\circ </math>, and that between triangle and square is <math> 144.7^\circ </math>. The dihedral angle of the cupolae and antiprism between two adjacent triangles and triangle-square is <math> 151.3^\circ </math> and <math>  141.6^\circ </math>, respectively.{{r|johnson}}

The gyroelongated square bicupola is one of five Johnson solids, which is [[chirality (mathematics)|chiral]], meaning that they have a "left-handed" and a "right-handed" form. In the following illustration, each square face on the left half of the figure is connected by a path of two triangular faces to a square face below it and on the left. In the figure of opposite chirality (the mirror image of the illustrated figure), each square on the left would be connected to a square face above it and on the right. These two chiral forms are not considered different Johnson solids.{{cn|date=January 2024|reason=The latter source mentions the symmetry, but it does not mention the property of chirality.}} It has the symmetry of [[dihedral group]] <math> D_4 </math>.{{r|johnson}}
